content.text:
## Findings

The mud is almost entirely **Kick + Sub Bass** stacking in the same band, with no separation when the full groove/drop is running.

**Levels (post-fader)**  
- **Sub Bass** is the loudest low-end source: sub 20–60 Hz at **−7.9 dB**, bass 60–150 Hz at **−10.8 dB**, integrated **−12.2 LUFS**, RMS **−10.9 dB**.  
- **Kick** sits under it in the same bands: sub **−10.4 dB**, bass **−13.2 dB**, **−13.5 LUFS**, RMS **−11.8 dB**.  
- Together they dump continuous energy into 20–150 Hz with no ducking between them.

**Why they collide**  
- Bass pattern `sub_line` is wall-to-wall: F1 (4 beats) → Ab1 (2) → C2 (2) over 2 bars — **no rests**.  
- Kick is four-on-the-floor every beat (`four_floor`).  
- Both hit **MIDI 36** on the last half of the bass loop (kick every beat as “C1” / bass “C2”), so fundamentals land on the **same pitch** regularly.  
- Bass chain is only **Saturator** at **+6 dB** analog clip — **no EQ, no highpass, no sidechain**. That drive thickens low-mids on top of the sub.  
- Kick EQ is only a **28 Hz** HPF — it keeps almost the entire sub and does not carve space for the bass.

**Not the problem**  
- **Stab**: HPF 150 Hz; sub/bass bands −55 / −38 dB.  
- **Dark Pad**: only in the **break** (bars 49–56) when kick/bass are out; HPF 120 Hz.  
- **Clap / Hats**: negligible below 150 Hz.  
- Master limiter (~2.5 dB GR) may glue the pile-up a bit but is not the cause.

Full-mix mud shows up from **groove** (bass+kick from bar 17; stab/clap from 33) and hardest in the **drop** (57–88) when everything runs together.

---

## Proposal

1. **Sub Bass › add Compressor** (before Saturator): sidechain from **Kick**, ratio **4:1**, threshold **−28 dB**, attack **1 ms**, release **80 ms**, knee soft — duck bass on each kick so the kick owns the punch.

2. **Sub Bass › add EQ Eight** (before Compressor):  
   - Band 1: **highpass**, **40 Hz**, **24 dB/oct** (kick keeps true sub).  
   - Band 2: **bell**, **cut −3 dB** at **65 Hz**, Q **1.2** (ease the shared fundamental with kick MIDI 36).

3. **Sub Bass › Saturator**: lower **driveDb** from **6** → **3** so saturation adds harmonics without bloating 100–300 Hz.

4. **Sub Bass › mixer**: volume **−1 dB → −3 dB** so kick leads the low end (bass was hotter in sub than kick).

5. **Kick › EQ Eight**: add band — **bell**, **cut −2 dB** at **100 Hz**, Q **1.0**, to open a pocket for bass body above the kick fundamental; keep the existing 28 Hz HPF.

No arrangement or MIDI pitch changes required unless you still want less unison on the C — in that case move the bass note at beat 6 from **C2 (36)** down to **Bb1 (34)** or up to **Eb2 (39)** so it stops locking to the kick fundamental.
